description: One thing worth knowing about a set of anchors, as data: the code says what, and the numbers say how much. Which numbers are set depends on the code.

anchors.description: The anchors the finding is about, by index.
anchors.title: anchors

code.description: What the finding is, as a stable code, and which numbers it sets: `too_few_distinct_anchors` (`count` distinct of `of` anchors), `duplicate_anchors` (`count` pairs), `low_ceiling` (`score`, the best any message can reach), `multiple_topics` (`count` topics), `misses_your_examples` and `misses_some_examples` (`count` of `of` examples match at `score`), `few_examples` (`count` of `of` examples match, too few to show more than `score` of such messages would; no `of` when there are none), `catching_the_rest_is_noisy` (catching them needs `score`, where `trafficCost` of ordinary traffic matches too), `false_alarms` (`count` of `of` counter-examples match at `score`), `few_counter_examples` (`count` of `of` counter-examples match, too few to rule out `score` of such messages matching; no `of` when there are none), `noisy_anchors` (`count` anchors, worst first in `anchors`; without the first the line could be `score` lower), `no_background`, and `background_resolution` (`count` messages cannot measure a `trafficCost` budget).
code.title: code

count.description: How many, for the codes that count something.
count.title: count

of.description: Out of how many, for the codes that count part of a whole.
of.title: of

score.description: The score the finding is about, on the threshold's scale, or for `few_examples` and `few_counter_examples` the share of messages the examples can vouch for.
score.title: score

severity.description: `Blocker` means it will not work and refuses activation, `Warn` means it will work badly and must be acknowledged, `Advice` is a call only the author can make.
severity.title: severity

trafficCost.description: The share of ordinary traffic the finding is about.
trafficCost.title: trafficCost

title: CorpusEvaluationFinding
